docs.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(heads,salaries) totals a payroll; divide by SUM(heads) for the cost per head
docs.explain:
SUMPRODUCT multiplies two ranges row by row, then adds the products. Given heads in B2:B5 and salaries in C2:C5, each team's headcount pairs with that team's salary before anything is summed. Three heads at 45000 come to 135000, and the four rows come to 345000.

The second screen divides that payroll by the total headcount, eight, and rounds: 345000 across eight heads is 43125. The divisor is SUM(B2:B5), so a team of three carries three times the weight of a team of one. Averaging the salary column gives 44000, a figure nobody on the sheet is paid.

Both ranges need the same shape; one that starts a row late pairs each salary with the wrong headcount, and the total still looks plausible. The divisor comes from the heads column: COUNT(B2:B5) counts four rows and would put the cost at 86250.

errors.text: The two ranges are different shapes, so the rows cannot be paired.
The headcount total is zero and the cost per head divides by it.
The divisor counts rows instead of heads, so four teams divide a payroll built on eight.

seo.title: Payroll total and cost per head in Excel
seo.description: SUMPRODUCT multiplies headcount by salary row by row in one call, and dividing that payroll by the headcount weighs teams the way the money does.
